skill.name: lark-apps
skill.description: Build, develop, publish, and operate Lark Miaoda applications through lark-cli, including databases, files, secrets, releases, access, and observability.
skill.summary: Guides end-to-end development and operations for Lark Miaoda applications.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, Chinese text entropy, relative documentation links, and defensive credential references. Confirmed risks include .env.local access, one-time raw API key output, and mandatory loading of hidden repository instructions. Semantic review also found automatic execution of dependency and development scripts from cloned repositories.

remediation.issue: Repository-provided SKILL.md files are treated as trusted instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Treat cloned instruction files as untrusted data. Extract only allowlisted plugin metadata, ignore behavioral directives, and surface suspicious instruction text before any tool use.

remediation.issue: The local flow executes npm install and npm run dev immediately after cloning.
remediation.suggestion: Review package.json and the lockfile first. Install with lifecycle scripts disabled, require confirmation for scripts, and execute development code in a restricted environment.

remediation.issue: Environment recovery writes and encourages direct reading of .env.local.
remediation.suggestion: Do not read secret values into agent context. Confirm before overwriting, enforce restrictive file permissions, and report only variable names and operation status.

remediation.issue: OpenAPI key creation and reset return a raw secret in command output.
remediation.suggestion: Route the one-time key directly to an approved secret manager. Keep it out of model transcripts, terminal history, logs, summaries, and cached command results.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Repository Instructions Are Loaded
semantic_findings.description: The local workflow requires reading a repository-provided SKILL.md after cloning. A compromised application repository can use that file to influence subsequent agent actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 39 makes reading the cloned repository instruction file mandatory and provides no trust-boundary or prompt-injection handling rule.

semantic_findings.title: Cloned Repository Code Executes Automatically
semantic_findings.description: The prescribed flow runs npm install and npm run dev in a newly cloned repository. Package lifecycle scripts or the development script can execute compromised repository code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly instruct both dependency installation and development-script execution without a manifest review, script suppression, confirmation, or sandbox requirement.

content.user_title: Build and Operate Lark Miaoda Apps
content.value_statement: Building and operating Miaoda apps requires specialized commands and safety checks. This skill guides development, deployment, data management, access, and observability through lark-cli.
actual_capabilities: Create, find, and update Lark Miaoda application records.
Publish static HTML sites and deploy full-stack application releases.
Initialize local repositories and guide cloud AI development sessions.
Manage application databases, stored files, environment variables, and access scopes.
Create and rotate application OpenAPI keys and manage capability plugins.
Query logs, traces, service metrics, and visitor analytics.
limitations: Requires an installed lark-cli and an authenticated Lark user with suitable scopes.
Does not manage Lark Drive files, Lark documents, or native Lark presentations.
Does not configure application roles, collaborator permissions, or automation rules.
Destructive database, secret, and production operations still require user review.

use_cases.title: Launch a Product Prototype
use_cases.description: Create a Miaoda app, choose local or cloud development, and publish a verified sharing link.

use_cases.title: Develop a Full-Stack Application
use_cases.description: Initialize the repository, implement changes, test with development data, and deploy the selected revision.

use_cases.title: Operate a Published Service
use_cases.description: Inspect releases, logs, traces, metrics, environment settings, files, and database state.

prompt_templates.title: Find an Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Find my Miaoda application named [name]. Show matching applications and ask me to choose when multiple results exist.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a Static Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish the static site in [directory] as a Miaoda HTML application. Check size limits and sensitive files before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Develop and Release an Existing App
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the Miaoda app [name or app_id] for local development. Implement [change], test it, then prepare a reviewed release.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Production Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [app_id] for [time range]. Correlate request volume, errors, latency, logs, traces, and recent releases without exposing secrets.

output_examples.input: Find the application named Team Check-in.
output_examples.output: I found two matching applications. Team Check-in Dev was updated today, and Team Check-in Archive was updated last month. Select one to continue.

output_examples.input: Publish the site in the dist directory.
output_examples.output: The size checks passed and no blocked credential files were detected. The site was published, and its access remains limited to the creator.

output_examples.input: Why did requests fail during the last hour?
output: Request failures increased after the latest release.
The affected endpoint also showed higher latency.
Review the cited release and trace records before rollback.

best_practices: Resolve the exact app_id before any write, deployment, or data operation.
Use development environments and dry runs before production or destructive actions.
Keep environment values, API keys, credentials, and signed links out of responses.
anti_patterns: Do not create a replacement application when the requested existing app is ambiguous.
Do not bypass confirmations for deletion, irreversible database work, or secret rotation.
Do not treat development links or historical publication flags as current release links.

faq.question: What is required before using this skill?
faq.answer: Install lark-cli and authenticate a Lark user that can access the target Miaoda applications.

faq.question: Can it create both static and full-stack applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports HTML applications, local full-stack development, and cloud AI development sessions.

faq.question: Can it publish a shareable link?
faq.answer: Yes. It publishes static sites or full-stack releases, then checks the application access scope.

faq.question: Can it manage production data?
faq.answer: Yes, with explicit environment selection, dry runs where supported, and confirmation for destructive actions.

faq.question: Does it reveal environment values or API keys?
faq.answer: It should not repeat secrets. Some commands access secret material, so secure storage and careful output handling remain necessary.

faq.question: Does it manage Lark documents or Drive files?
faq.answer: No. Use dedicated Lark Drive, document, or presentation skills for those resources.
